summary: Mount Hood NF lookout site in Wasco County: a 1920s rag camp, then pole, L-6 and R-6 towers; the last tower was lost in a 1994 lift attempt and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Successive towers: 40-ft pole L-4 (about 1937), 82-ft treated timber L-6 (1940s), 84-ft treated timber R-6 with flat cab (1962)
facts.status_note: The last tower was destroyed in 1994 during an attempt to move its cab and top half; FFLA lists it as gone

staffing.status: deactivated in 1964 (county listing); a 1936 telephone ring was assigned to the station

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mount Hood National Forest)

events.note: Developed as a rag camp; sources give only the 1920s, so the year is the decade start
Oregonian item quoted on the county listing: a new ladder and platform, 130 feet high, at Post Point; does not match the 40-ft pole tower story
Panorama photographs taken by Robert Snyder, per county listing
Assigned telephone ring for this station, per county listing
82-ft treated timber L-6 tower; sources give only the 1940s
84-ft treated timber R-6 tower with flat cab
Attempt to lift cab and top half six miles east to become a rental failed; the load was dropped after lifting from the lower tower. Firelookout.com and county listing say destroyed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, US 639 / OR 71

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS and firelookout.com pages describe a 40-ft pole tower around 1937; a 1932 Oregonian item quoted on the county listing describes a 130-ft ladder and platform. The story reports both and does not pick one.

The FFLOS page says the tower was removed; firelookout.com and the county listing say destroyed. The story uses the removal attempt described on FFLOS and notes the destruction in the other two sources.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: coordinates, elevation and FFLOS registration match. No access source found, so no access key. No source describes the site today. Staffing evidence is limited to a 1936 telephone ring and a 1964 deactivation; no staff are named. The 1920s camp, 1932 ladder and 1937 pole tower cannot all be reconciled from these sources. The brief's access 'unknown' is left as is.
